decisions.reason: As a stand-alone multi-model product line that builds directly on the established portfolio, it embodies visible investment and strategic continuity, so management is unlikely to abandon it and can still interpret any softer demand as normal adoption timing.

This service is less prominently committed than the main product lines, but because it supports enterprise integration around the firm's geospatial stack, management is still inclined to continue and justify prior development rather than withdraw quickly.

An open GIS application development framework is highly aligned with the firm's open, extensible and user-centered direction, and the sunk development effort behind a product line makes continued backing more likely than exit.

The explicit launch communication and its close fit with GIS application integration create a public and strategic commitment that makes management more likely to keep refining the service than remove it within a year.

Although a workshop format is easier to scale back than software products, it has its own page, builds on the established consulting business and is still early enough for management to attribute uneven uptake to market ramp-up rather than product failure.
